scope: secret scanning of worktree and git history
sql injection and ssrf candidate review
frontend and backend image build, runtime probes, and Trivy image scanning

findings.evidence: Initial Trivy DS-0002 finding; final Trivy filesystem scan reports zero misconfigurations.
findings.impact: A compromise of nginx runs with unnecessary container privileges.
findings.remediation: Implemented USER nginx, container port 8080, writable nginx runtime directories, and synchronized Compose mappings and health checks.

findings.evidence: Initial 26 Semgrep github-actions-mutable-action-tag findings; final scan reports zero.
findings.impact: Mutable action tags can resolve to unreviewed code.
findings.remediation: Pinned all 26 action references to the current official tag commit SHAs and retained version comments.

findings.impact: Untrusted multimodal contexts may trigger SSRF or local file reads.
findings.remediation: Keep Ragas out of production, use it only in an isolated offline evaluation environment, and upgrade or remove it when a complete upstream fix exists.

findings.location: backend/rag and backend/services raw SQL call sites
findings.evidence: 12 Semgrep ERROR candidates and 11 Bandit B608 candidates
findings.impact: Future changes could introduce injection if untrusted values reach SQL structure.
findings.remediation: Retain parameter binding and identifier allowlists; add focused tests whenever query composition changes.

findings.location: Dockerfile and frontend-vue/Dockerfile base image declarations
findings.evidence: Python, Node and Nginx images are pinned to the exact digests used by the successful runtime and image scan probes.
findings.impact: Mutable base image tags could otherwise drift to unreviewed build inputs.
findings.remediation: Implemented digest pinning; update digests only together with image rebuild, runtime probes and Trivy scans.

findings.location: Dockerfile:3 pinned Python 3.11 slim base image (Debian 13.6)
findings.evidence: trivy-backend-hardened-final-image.json reports 4 Critical perl-base advisories and 19 High OS-package advisories; every Critical/High entry has an empty FixedVersion. No Python package vulnerabilities remain in the runtime image.
findings.impact: Affected base utilities and libraries have potential memory-corruption, archive traversal, arbitrary file modification and denial-of-service paths if their vulnerable functionality becomes attacker-reachable.
findings.remediation: Track Debian 13 security updates and rebuild on a corrected digest when available. Retain non-root execution and least privilege. A current bookworm comparison was worse at 6 Critical and 20 High, so no downgrade was made.

findings.evidence: Compose does not uniformly set no-new-privileges, capability drops or read-only root filesystems.
findings.impact: A compromised process retains more runtime capability than necessary.
findings.remediation: Design service-specific controls after enumerating required writable paths for Postgres, backend and Nginx.
